stories.label: Live Updates: FAA Declares Nationwide Ground Stop of Flights
stories.summary: Every departing flight in the US was grounded after 'a communication issue impacting all Air Route Traffic Control Centers', per Transportation Secretary Sean Duffy; The War Zone notes it is only the third nationwide ground stop in FAA history. Lead with the single point of failure: one communications fault halted the world's largest airspace. Say what is known of the cause and what is not, and who is stranded abroad as connections collapse.

stories.label: Suspected Drones Over RAF Lakenheath Just Triggered Security Response: U.S. Air Force
stories.summary: Suspected drones over RAF Lakenheath, the main US fighter base in England, set off a security response after some USAF aircraft had already been moved out of England and base threat levels raised. Lead with the evacuation and raised threat level: the Iran war's reach now extends to US bases in Europe. Report only what the Air Force has confirmed, and do not attribute the drones to anyone without evidence.

stories.label: Tinubu booed at Abuja mosque after Friday prayers
stories.summary: Worshippers at Abuja's Shehu Shagari National Mosque chanted against President Bola Tinubu as his convoy left Friday prayers. Videos were obtained by Premium Times. Lead with the setting: open dissent at the capital's central mosque, a few feet from the president. Explain what the crowd was angry about (cost of living, insecurity, whatever the report names) and how the presidency responded.

stories.label: North accounts for most of Nigeria's recorded maternal deaths - Report
stories.summary: The government's own 2026 Joint Annual Review statistics put about three-quarters of maternal deaths recorded in health facilities in the Northwest and Northeast. Lead with that share against those zones' share of the population. Explain the mechanism: insurgency, facility gaps and births outside clinics, which also means the recorded figure understates the toll. Nigeria accounts for a large share of the world's maternal deaths.

stories.label: Local Journalist Murdered After BBC Documentary Exposed Police Corruption in Ecuador
stories.summary: A local Ecuadorian journalist was killed after a BBC documentary exposed police corruption. Lead with the victim's name and the link to the documentary. The mechanism is accountability: under Noboa's militarised 'internal armed conflict' the security forces are the subject of the reporting, and local journalists, not the foreign broadcaster, bear the risk. Name what the documentary alleged and whether anyone has been charged.

stories.label: TASS expelled from European news alliance without reason
stories.summary: The European Alliance of News Agencies' General Assembly expelled Russia's state agency TASS in a secret ballot. TASS had been suspended since February 2022, and expulsion votes needing a three-quarters majority failed in 2022 and 2024. Lead with what changed between those failed votes and this one. Attribute everything to Russian state news agency TASS, including Zakharova's 'that's what they deserve', and give EANA's stated position if TASS reports one. The only sources are TASS.

stories.label: Finance must break developing countries from 'debt and disaster' loop - UN climate chief
stories.summary: At COP31, UN climate chief Simon Stiell told ministers that hitting a headline finance figure will not lift developing countries out of a cycle of borrowing to rebuild after disasters, then borrowing again. Lead with the mechanism: climate finance delivered as loans adds to the debt of the countries that emitted least. Name the targets on the table and which countries are pushing for grants over loans.

stories.label: How Jensen Huang's exit from Nvidia impacts China's AI supply chain
stories.summary: This is a new angle on Huang's resignation, not a recap: Beijing loses its most important advocate in Silicon Valley, Chinese buyers are stockpiling chips ahead of a successor who may be less willing to lobby against export controls, and Taiwanese and Southeast Asian suppliers are bracing. Lead with the stockpiling and what it shows about China's dependence on one company's political posture.

stories.label: Trump Jr. out as Kalshi advisor after his firm's big investment in Polymarket
stories.summary: Donald Trump Jr. held equity as a Kalshi adviser while his father's administration sided with Kalshi in its lawsuits against state regulators. He left only after his venture firm made a large investment in its rival Polymarket. Lead with the conflict: the president's son has stakes on both sides of an industry the administration regulates and defends in court. Name the size of the investment and the federal agency positions involved.

stories.label: In elephants, the resilience of communities has its limits
stories.summary: A long-term study of Asian elephants in a Sri Lankan national park (UC San Diego) finds that ecological change is shrinking the population and that the social networks that normally absorb deaths and departures have a breaking point. Lead with the measured decline and the mechanism by which habitat change frays the social structure. Name the park and the study.

stories.label: Modified $450 3D printer builds living materials with more than 100 layers
stories.summary: Researchers turned a $450 consumer 3D printer into one that prints living bacterial materials more than 100 layers thick. Such materials can clean contaminated water or break down plastic. Lead with the price: a technique confined to specialist bioprinters now runs on commodity hardware, which opens it to labs in poorer countries. Name the institution, the journal and what the materials were shown to do.

stories.label: FBI flash alert says Artex tool automating cyberattacks at 'machine speed'
stories.summary: An FBI flash alert warns that Artex, an open-source AI-driven hacking tool, chains attack techniques automatically, taking some intrusions from first targeting to privileged access in under three hours. Lead with the three hours: defenders' detection windows are measured in days. Name who has used it, which sectors were hit and the mitigations the FBI lists. (A fourth US dateline: no non-US security story in the feed matches it.)

stories.label: 阿里发布AI音乐App，我用它写了首黄仁勋告别曲
stories.summary: Alibaba released HappyShrimp (快乐虾米), its AI music app, on iOS and Android, three months after the HappyShrimp 1.0 model launched on the web. It writes lyrics, composes, arranges and sings a three-minute song in about a minute from a description. Lead with Zhidx's test, which wrote a farewell song to Jensen Huang from that day's news: the app searches current events. Note the 'make the same' remix feature and the mainland view that the vocals still sound synthetic.

stories.label: While Russia tries to manipulate information, local civil society is teaching Armenians media literacy
stories.summary: As Armenia moves away from its long reliance on Russia, it is the target of generative-AI disinformation campaigns, and local groups such as iVerify Armenia are running fact-checking and media-literacy programmes. Lead with a documented example of a fabricated item and how it spread. The mechanism is that AI cuts the cost of tailored propaganda, and the counter is local and under-resourced.

stories.label: Israeli strike on Nasser Hospital in Gaza kills six, disables key medical departments
stories.summary: An Israeli strike on Nasser Hospital in Khan Younis killed six people and knocked out a surgical unit and other key departments, in southern Gaza's main remaining referral hospital. Lead with the dead and the departments lost: the strike lands in the same week as Gaza's first winter hypothermia death of an infant, so a besieged population loses surgical care exactly as cold-weather casualties start. Name who struck and who died; the mechanism is the systematic dismantling of Gaza's health system.

stories.label: Turkiye, Qatar sign defence agreement: Turkish presidency
stories.summary: Erdogan and Emir Tamim signed a new defence agreement in Istanbul, deepening an alliance that already puts a Turkish base on Qatari soil. The angle: with the Iran war, IRGC strikes on Bahrain and mines in Hormuz, Gulf states are hedging away from sole reliance on US protection — explain what Turkey gives Qatar (troops, drones, a non-US guarantor) and what Qatar gives Turkey (money and a Gulf foothold).

stories.label: Lebanese military discovers weapons depot in southern Beirut
stories.summary: Lebanese army intelligence raided a large weapons depot, presumably Hezbollah's, in Beirut's southern suburbs (Musharafieh). Only Russian state news agency TASS carries it, so attribute it and do not state ownership as fact. The mechanism: the Lebanese state disarming Hezbollah in its own heartland is the test of the ceasefire terms — say who demands disarmament and what Lebanon risks internally.

stories.label: UAE remains 'main destination' for gold smuggled out of Sudan and other war zones
stories.summary: A Swissaid report finds the UAE imported at least 591 tonnes of illicit gold in 2024, much of it from Sudan, where gold finances the RSF's war. Lead with the 591 tonnes and the route: mines in RSF-held Darfur to Dubai refineries to the world market, despite UAE due-diligence rules. Name the price of gold as the series — record prices raise the payoff of every smuggled kilo, and Sudanese civilians bear the cost.

stories.label: German coalition disagreements hold up ECB jobs deal
stories.summary: Merz and his finance minister cannot agree on a German candidate for one of three vacant ECB executive board seats, stalling a package deal among eurozone capitals; Merz says Berlin will name someone next week. The mechanism: who sits on the board sets the ECB's rate path at a moment when Italy's bank levies and sovereign debt worries are on the table — tie it to the ECB policy rate and explain how board seats are traded among Germany, France and the rest.

stories.label: Copper, gold deposits identified at eight sites in Balochistan's Chagai district: mining company
stories.summary: Pakistan's National Resources Limited says nearly 25,000 metres of drilling found copper and gold at eight sites in Chagai, Balochistan, and it is moving toward a first resource estimate. New since our minerals-forum story: drill results, not pledges. The angle: Balochistan's mineral wealth (Reko Diq is next door) is pitched to Gulf, US and Chinese investors while the province stays Pakistan's poorest and an insurgency targets extraction. Name copper and gold as the series.

stories.label: Bitcoin's six-week slide draws parallels with sell-off before SpaceX IPO
stories.summary: Bitcoin fell to about $68,000, its lowest since August and below its 200-week moving average, heading for a sixth straight weekly loss — down 11% in November. New since our sub-$70,000 story: the streak and the cause CoinDesk names, money leaving crypto for Anthropic's oversubscribed IPO, as it did before SpaceX's June listing, plus a strong dollar and Fed-hike risk. Name bitcoin as the series; lead with the capital rotation, not the price.

stories.label: Global wind farms are associated with land use dependent asymmetric warming and ecological changes
stories.summary: A global study in Communications Earth & Environment finds wind farms warm their surroundings unevenly — the effect depends on whether turbines stand on cropland, grassland or forest — with measurable ecological change. Lead with the asymmetry (night versus day, or by land type, whichever the paper quantifies). The surprise for the reader: clean energy has a local climate footprint, which matters for siting as wind expands across the Global South.

stories.label: Did El Niño cause an early breakdown in the polar vortex? | New Scientist
stories.summary: The stratospheric polar vortex has weakened unprecedentedly early, and some scientists suspect the record El Niño is the cause. Explain the teleconnection — how warm Pacific water disturbs winds 30 km above the Arctic — and what follows: a likely cold, snowy European winter just as gas is dear from the Iran war. Keep the attribution as a hypothesis; name natural gas as the series.

stories.label: Doctors have questions about the Watchman. Boston Scientific has a sales pitch.
stories.summary: A STAT investigation into Boston Scientific's Watchman heart implant, put into more than 800,000 patients worldwide: the company's marketing runs ahead of the evidence that the device beats blood thinners. Lead with the 800,000 implants and the gap between the trial data and the sales pitch. Accountability: name the FDA's role and what doctors are told versus what the studies show.

stories.label: 梁圣再放大招：人人都能手搓DeepSeek App了
stories.summary: DeepSeek opened its whole app stack as an API — web search, search during reasoning, file parsing, URL reading, OCR, speech and safety checks — so developers can rebuild the DeepSeek app one-for-one, paying tool fees on top of tokens. The angle: a Chinese lab turning its consumer product into infrastructure, and the notable clause that developers serving outside users must run the safety check and meet China's content-review, model-registration and AI-labelling duties — Beijing's regulation shipped inside the API.

stories.label: China’s Internet Giants Are Listing AI Units Because the Parent Stock Will Not Price Them
stories.summary: Alibaba, Baidu and Kuaishou are spinning chip and model units onto separate markets because their parents' shares do not price the AI assets. Builds on our Alibaba T-Head IPO story with the pattern across three giants. The mechanism: a spin-off buys a public price tag and raises capital under US chip export controls, but the cost and the control stay with the parent — say who gains (parent holders, Beijing's self-reliance push) and the risk to new investors.

stories.label: Windows 0-day dropped by disgruntled researcher hands hackers System rights
stories.summary: The researcher known as Nightmare Eclipse, publicly feuding with Microsoft, has released another unpatched Windows zero-day, SignDrop, which gives any local user System rights. Lead with the fact that it is public and unpatched: every Windows machine is exposed until Microsoft ships a fix, in the same week as its global 365 outage. The structural point: a broken bug-bounty relationship turns disclosure into a weapon, and users carry the risk.

stories.label: UN watchdog calls on Iran to reopen nuclear facilities to inspection
stories.summary: New development on the Iran nuclear arc: the IAEA formally urged Tehran to restore inspector access, and Iran replied that inspections are impossible 'in the current security situation' — while bombed sites like Isfahan hold enriched uranium no one can verify. Tie it to the Assembly of Experts' NPT-withdrawal debate covered this week: the inspection gap is the mechanism by which the war removes the one external check on the stockpile. Dateline Vienna or Tehran per the source.

stories.label: First child death from hypothermia recorded in Gaza -- Health Ministry
stories.summary: A nine-month-old, Kinan Ahmad Arkik, died of severe hypothermia in Gaza — the season's first cold death, per the Gaza Health Ministry. Name the child and lead with the cause: displaced families in tents without fuel or shelter materials because entry of supplies is restricted; winter has barely begun. The continuation of the siege is the development. Only source is Russian state agency TASS relaying the ministry — attribute it ('the Gaza Health Ministry said, according to Russian state news agency TASS') and do not state beyond that. Dateline Gaza City.

stories.label: Russia hit by second car bomb in as many days as peace talks continue
stories.summary: A car bomb in Moscow injured Sergei Zavorotny, a former adviser to Ukraine's exiled pro-Kremlin ex-PM Mykola Azarov — the second car bombing in Russia in two days (the first in St Petersburg). The structural point: a campaign of targeted killings inside Russia running in parallel with peace talks, and what it does to the negotiating climate. Say who is suspected and who has claimed nothing; attribute Investigative Committee claims. Dateline Moscow.

stories.label: Revealed: The UK charities funding Israeli schools in illegally occupied Palestine
stories.summary: UK-registered charities, carrying tax relief, are funding Israeli schools in occupied East Jerusalem that take pupils on tours of illegal settlements, one with links to the Israeli army. Accountability mechanism: British taxpayers subsidise, via Gift Aid and charity status, institutions embedded in an occupation the UK itself calls illegal. Name the charities and amounts from the filings; state what the Charity Commission rules require. Declassified is an advocacy outlet — rest every claim on the charity records it cites and attribute. Dateline East Jerusalem.

stories.label: Russia Oil Revenues Hit Five-Month High on Crude Rally, IEA Says
stories.summary: The IEA's monthly report: Russia earned about $21.2bn from crude and product exports in October, up ~65% on a year earlier, because the Iran war lifted Brent crude — and the same report says the oil market returns to surplus for the first time since the war began. Lead with the transfer: a Gulf war is financing Moscow's war in Ukraine. Name Brent crude as the series. Dateline Paris.

stories.label: 'Nobody owes anybody permanent fixture on currency' - Kwakye Ofosu on removal of Big Six
stories.summary: The Bank of Ghana is issuing a new 'Heritage Series' of smaller, harder-to-forge cedi notes, and the redesign drops five of the Big Six founding nationalists, keeping only Nkrumah — the government says no one is owed a permanent place. Lead with the counterfeiting mechanism and the cost of reissuing a currency, then the fight over who a nation puts on its money. Note when the notes enter circulation. Dateline Accra.

stories.label: Kazakh president says arrest of sovereign wealth fund chief will not disrupt its operations
stories.summary: Kazakhstan's security service arrested the head of Samruk-Kazyna — the sovereign fund that owns the national railway, oil and uranium champions — on corruption suspicion, and Tokayev says it won't disrupt operations. Lead with the scale of what the fund controls and who now runs it; the structural question is whether this is accountability or a reshuffle of control over state assets. Dateline Astana.

stories.label: Одним графиком: Как война России с Украиной поднимает цены на бензин в Кыргызстане
stories.summary: Kloop's data analysis: fuel prices in Kyrgyzstan have nearly tripled in six years, and Ukraine's drone strikes on Russian refineries — which caused a new fuel crisis in Russia this November — will push them higher, because Kyrgyzstan imports almost all its fuel from Russia and its economy moves by truck. Lead with the tripling and the single-supplier dependency: a war 3,000 km away sets the price of bread in Bishkek. Dateline Bishkek.

stories.label: Nvidia fallout throws spotlight on Southeast Asia's AI boom
stories.summary: Material new development on the Nvidia arc: reporting that Jensen Huang's exit followed an affair with a suspected Chinese spy has put Singapore and Malaysia's chip and data-centre hubs under scrutiny, as US lawmakers of both parties push tougher export restrictions — and Nvidia has lost nearly $2tn in value. Lead with who pays: Malaysia's Johor data-centre build-out, which depends on Nvidia chips being allowed in. Dateline Singapore.

stories.label: Quantum Systems drones back in the air after malware scare
stories.summary: A malicious software update reportedly reached military servers at drone maker Quantum Systems, and the Bundeswehr grounded its drones as a precaution; they fly again now. Lead with the supply-chain mechanism: a vendor's update channel is a path into the armed forces — and the same drones fly for Ukraine. Say what is confirmed and what is 'reportedly'. Dateline Munich.

stories.label: Bundeshaushalt: Bund verschleiert KI-Ausgaben
stories.summary: Germany's federal AI taskforce is meant to make the country an 'AI nation' by 2030, but netzpolitik.org finds the federal budget does not show how much Berlin spends on AI or how Digital Minister Karsten Wildberger will fund the plan. Lead with the accountability gap: a national strategy with no traceable line in the budget parliament votes on. Use any figures the piece extracts. Dateline Berlin.

stories.label: This AI 'mechanic' can peer inside the black box of other neural networks
stories.summary: MIT researchers used one AI model to read and edit the internal workings of another network directly, instead of retraining it — a new route into the 'black box'. Lead with what the 'mechanic' actually changed and how they checked it worked; note it is a preprint, not yet peer-reviewed. Why it matters: interpretability is the condition for auditing systems now deployed in courts, hiring and weapons. Dateline Cambridge, Massachusetts.

stories.label: Oʻahu infrastructure threatened by tipping point in sea-level rise impacts
stories.summary: A University of Hawaiʻi study finds models that count only rising seawater drastically underestimate the threat to coastal infrastructure, and identifies a tipping point after which impacts accelerate. Name from the source which other mechanisms (e.g. groundwater rise, drainage backflow) the study adds — do not assume them. Lead with the size of the underestimate and the threshold; the finding generalises to every low-lying coastal city on porous ground. Dateline Honolulu.

stories.label: Brent crude rises over 1.6% on ICE after Trump's remarks on Iran deal
stories.summary: Trump said there is 'no need for a deal with Iran', and Brent crude and WTI rose more than 1% as traders priced a longer war in the Gulf. The cause is the story: the diplomatic exit is closing (prediction-market odds of a senior US-Iran meeting by 30 November fell from 26% to 10% in a week). Say who pays for dearer oil: importers in South Asia and Africa, not Washington. Name Brent crude.

stories.label: Asean faces Myanmar dilemma as some members pursue closer ties
stories.summary: Thailand and other members want ASEAN's upcoming summit to lift the five-year ban on Myanmar's junta leaders attending high-level meetings, though the civil war goes on. Lead with the bargain: engagement for trade and border stability against accountability for the 2021 coup and for the Rohingya. Say who gains a seat (Min Aung Hlaing) and who bears the cost (civilians under airstrikes).

stories.label: US reports record number of deportations and arrests in 2026
stories.summary: DHS says ICE carried out 483,200 deportations in fiscal 2026, a record, and set a new high for arrests. Lead with the number, then the mechanism: how the arrests are made and who is held. Democrats are preparing to investigate the tactics after the midterms. Name the countries most of the deportees go to, where the source gives them.

stories.label: Bridge damage disrupts transport links across Dnieper in Kiev -- lawmaker
stories.summary: A Ukrainian MP, Dmitry Razumkov, says severe damage to two bridges over the Dnieper has cut road links between the two halves of Kyiv. The reader should learn what a city of three million loses when its river crossings fail. Only Russian state news agency TASS carries it, so attribute it to Razumkov via TASS and do not state the cause as fact. Datelined Kyiv.

stories.label: India's exports jump 29.9% to $89.99 billion in October, trade deficit narrows
stories.summary: India's exports of goods and services rose 29.9% year on year to $89.99bn in October, and the trade deficit narrowed to $20.09bn, even with the Gulf war raising oil import costs and inflation at 6.09%. Lead with what drove the jump (which sectors, which markets) and what it means for the rupee and the RBI's rate decision.

stories.label: Pakistan's mineral exploration increasingly focused on strategic resources, minister tells investors
stories.summary: At the Pakistan Minerals Investment Forum in Islamabad, the petroleum minister pitched copper and other strategic minerals to foreign delegations. Lead with who is buying in (which states and firms, what stakes) and who holds the ground: much of the copper and gold is in Balochistan, where local communities have long said they get little from the extraction.

stories.label: 6倍认购，史上最大IPO遭疯抢！达里奥将做客直播间
stories.summary: Anthropic's IPO is about six times oversubscribed. With a $26bn private placement alongside it, the company could raise up to $90.4bn at about a $1.4tn valuation, the largest listing on record. Lead with the circularity: Nvidia and Google put in $10bn each, and AMD, Broadcom, Micron, Microsoft and TSMC also buy in. These are the suppliers Anthropic has committed about $895bn of future compute purchases to, roughly ten times what it raises. Note that the Nvidia stake comes as Huang has just resigned. Disclose that Anthropic makes the Claude models zuhd.news uses.

stories.label: Alibaba’s Chip Unit Wants to Go Public. Who Pays It?
stories.summary: Alibaba's T-Head chip unit is preparing a Hong Kong IPO, and Alibaba says more than 60% of its computing capacity serves customers outside the group, such as carmakers that rent its Zhenwu chips through Alibaba Cloud. Lead with the business model: China's answer to US export controls is selling domestic AI silicon as rented cloud compute, not as chips. The question is whether outside demand is real or routed through Alibaba's own cloud.

stories.label: DJI to revise prices on some products as chip and memory costs climb
stories.summary: DJI, the world's dominant drone maker, will raise suggested retail prices on some products from 18 November, citing sustained rises in semiconductor and memory costs. Lead with the mechanism: AI data centres are absorbing the world's memory supply, and the cost is now reaching consumer hardware. Drones are also front-line equipment in Ukraine, Sudan and Myanmar.

stories.label: ESA's Euclid telescope maps over 900 million galaxies
stories.summary: ESA has released Euclid's first large data set: more than 900 million galaxies mapped to trace the large-scale structure of the universe, and with it dark matter and dark energy. Lead with the scale and with what the map can test that earlier surveys could not, such as gravitational lensing across a third of the sky. Explain the mechanism plainly.

stories.label: 5 takeaways from STAT's investigation of the sprawling 'three-parent IVF' industry
stories.summary: A STAT investigation finds that mitochondrial replacement therapy ('three-parent IVF') is being sold across borders to older women as a fertility treatment, despite scientific and ethical concerns and little evidence it works for them. Lead with the science: what MRT was designed for (preventing mitochondrial disease) and why using it for age-related infertility is unproven. Then the accountability: which companies sell it, in which countries, to whom, and why regulators do not reach them.

stories.label: G7 repeats US falsehoods about Cuba: Cuban FM
stories.summary: Trump says he would consider a military campaign to topple Cuba's government before leaving office, hours after ordering JD Vance to abandon ceasefire talks with Tehran. Lead with the threat against an island the US has already cut off from the world's oil (mint: Cuba now runs on American fuel); Cuba's foreign minister says the G7 is repeating US falsehoods. Datelined Havana: the policy lands there.

stories.label: IRGC destroys U.S. early warning radar in Bahrain
stories.summary: Iranian state news agency Mehr reports the IRGC Aerospace Force struck a US early-warning radar in Bahrain, in retaliation for a US air attack on a telecommunications tower in Sirik, and threatens a 'limitless response' to further strikes. State-media only: attribute every claim to the IRGC via Mehr. The structural point: a tit-for-tat on infrastructure while the ceasefire is untested and Washington has just pulled Vance from the talks — Bahrain, a Gulf host of US forces, carries the cost. Datelined Manama.

stories.label: How medical neglect killed Alfredo Díaz in a Venezuelan cell
stories.summary: A UN report documents how medical neglect in state custody killed opposition politician and former regional governor Alfredo Díaz, and finds Venezuela's repressive apparatus still active despite the government's shifts and the new US oil deal. Lead with the named victim and the named custodians; the accountability gap is that a détente with Washington has not reached the cells.

stories.label: Indian Markets Open Lower Amid Inflation And Rate Hike Concerns Today
stories.summary: India's retail inflation surged to 6.09% in October, above the RBI's 6% tolerance ceiling, and markets now price a policy rate hike next month. Lead with the inflation figure, not the Sensex: the mechanism is imported oil through a closed Strait of Hormuz feeding into prices for 1.4 billion people. Name the series: Brent crude.

stories.label: Intesa criticises Italy for bank levies in 2027 budget, says ECB may intervene
stories.summary: Italy's largest bank warns Rome's punitive bank levies in the 2027 budget could push the ECB to order Italian lenders to cut their sovereign-debt holdings. The mechanism to explain: Italian banks are the biggest buyers of Italian government bonds, so taxing them risks weakening the state's own funding — the doom loop in reverse.

stories.label: BTC news: Prices slip below $70K, triggering $1.2 billion in liquidations
stories.summary: Bitcoin fell below $70,000 for the first time since August, forcing exchanges to liquidate more than $1.3 billion of leveraged futures in 24 hours. The cause is the story: rising bond yields on expected Fed hikes (New York Fed's Williams called inflation 'far too high' last night) punish non-yielding assets. Name the series: bitcoin and the US 10-year Treasury yield.

stories.label: US disrupts North Korea's $400 million crypto scam, FBI says
stories.summary: The Justice Department seized cloud servers behind a North Korean operation that used fake video meetings and deepfaked faces ('FaceStealer') to steal over $400 million in crypto, and moved to seize $1.2 billion taken from Binance. Lead with the technique: deepfaked video calls as the attack vector against developers and exchange staff, funding a sanctioned state's weapons programme.

stories.label: Organizações lançam carta defendendo projeto que regula mercados digitais
stories.summary: Brazilian civil-society groups launched a letter backing PL 4.675, the bill to regulate digital markets and big-tech platforms, while deputies aligned with the tech companies brand it 'censorship 2.0'. Lead with the fight over framing: competition law recast as speech control, the same playbook used against Brazil's platform rules before. Datelined Brasília.

stories.label: US nonprofits sue tech giants to halt AI development
stories.summary: A coalition of consumer and digital-safety watchdogs including Public Citizen has sued OpenAI, Google, Meta and other leading labs in California, asking a court to freeze training and deployment of 'catastrophic' AI models. Lead with the remedy sought — a court-ordered training freeze has no precedent — and the legal theory that carries it.

stories.label: Elon Musk's SpaceX plans over $74 billion in AI computing campuses across Texas and Arizona, including a $50 billion proposal that promises 6,500 jobs but faces opposition from 2,400 local petition signers
stories.summary: SpaceX plans more than $74 billion of AI computing campuses in Texas and Arizona, one $50 billion site promising 6,500 jobs against 2,400 local petition signers, while Bloomberg reports (via TASS) that SpaceX and Tesla may announce a merger in December, the largest deal in history. Lead with SpaceX turning from rockets into an AI-compute company; the local opposition is about water and power. Datelined Brownsville.

stories.label: Trump threatens to double tariffs on Mexico if migrant caravans not stopped
stories.summary: Datelined in Mexico, where it lands: days after Republican midterm losses, Trump makes tariff policy hostage to migration enforcement, threatening to double duties unless Mexico halts a caravan that set out from its southern border. Lead with the mechanism: trade leverage outsources border policing to Sheinbaum's government. Name who pays: Mexican exporters and the migrants pushed back south. Al Jazeera's report on the caravan's departure gives the migrants' side.

stories.label: Burnham Warns of Long Nights Ahead as UK-EU Summit Looms
stories.summary: More than 40 European leaders meet in Dublin for the European Political Community. The agenda is the rising count of hybrid attacks across the continent (sabotage, drones, bomb threats) and whether Europe can name one envoy for the Ukraine peace talks the US is running without it. The structural why: Europe pays for the war but has no seat at the table. Bloomberg adds the UK-EU reset strain.

stories.label: European Commission demands urgent restoration of Starshield in Ukraine
stories.summary: The new development since this morning's story: the European Commission now formally demands that SpaceX restore Starshield. Zelenskiy says the disruption has run for several days along the whole front line and in occupied areas, and SpaceX tells Ars Technica that nothing is restricted. Lead with the accountability gap: one private company's switch decides a front's communications while US envoys negotiate in Moscow, and Brussels has no lever but a statement.

stories.label: Intelligence testimony reveals mafia-like networks, corruption and political interference inside government
stories.summary: South Africa's acting intelligence coordinator, Dr Ntandazo Sifolo, testified under oath that successive intelligence assessments warned criminal syndicates and political interference were contaminating police and prosecutors, and that the warnings went unheeded. The accountability angle: the state's own spies documented the capture, and the question is who received the assessments and did nothing.

stories.label: MK, EFF, SACP form block to drive municipal agendas, with conditional support for ANC
stories.summary: After the municipal vote, MK, the EFF and the SACP form a 'Council of the Left' holding about 20% of the vote, and will back the ANC only if it leaves its national coalition with the DA and Freedom Front Plus. Lead with the leverage: city coalitions such as Johannesburg's mayoralty now hinge on a bloc trying to break the national government of national unity. Polymarket odds on Helen Zille as Johannesburg mayor fell from 56% to 38% this week.

stories.label: Trinbagonian Jason Jones wins landmark Privy Council judgement deeming ‘buggery laws’ unconstitutional
stories.summary: London's Privy Council, still the final court for Trinidad and Tobago, overturned a 2025 appeal ruling and struck down the country's colonial-era sodomy law after a decade-long case. Lead with the precedent and the mechanism: a court in the former imperial capital rules on a colonial statute, and its reasoning on 'savings clauses' that shield pre-independence laws applies across other Commonwealth Caribbean states that still send final appeals to London.

stories.label: Brazilian Inflation Ticks Up After Lula's Win Rattles Markets
stories.summary: Brazil's annual inflation rose to 4.63% in October, further above target though below forecasts. It arrives as markets sell off on Lula's re-election and a widening budget gap. Lead with the mechanism: a weaker real and fiscal doubts feed into prices, so the central bank keeps Selic rates high and Brazilian borrowers pay for it. Reuters adds the ECB, set for its last hike in December, as the global backdrop of tightening.

stories.label: Mercedes-Benz to halt 'all future investments' in Germany
stories.summary: Mercedes-Benz halts all further investment in Germany and puts plant closures on the table, escalating its fight with IG Metall and the works councils over labour costs. Lead with the threat itself: Germany's flagship carmaker uses capital flight as a bargaining weapon. The structural why is Chinese competition and high energy costs hollowing out German manufacturing, and the people it lands on are tens of thousands of workers in Stuttgart and Sindelfingen.

stories.label: How Emefiele allegedly acquired multi-billion-naira properties through proxies - Witness
stories.summary: An EFCC witness testifies that former central bank governor Godwin Emefiele built a dollar-rationing system that shut ordinary Nigerians and businesses out of the official forex window, pushing them into 'special arrangements', while he acquired multi-billion-naira properties through proxies. Lead with the mechanism: scarcity of dollars at the official rate became a source of rent. Tie it to the naira's collapse after the window was unified, which ordinary Nigerians paid for.

stories.label: Makinde's campaign group demands probe of Tinubu's N11.2trn crude oil-backed loans
stories.summary: Nigeria has borrowed N11.2 trillion against future crude oil, and the lenders, interest rates, fees and the volume of oil pledged have not been disclosed. Oyo governor Seyi Makinde's presidential campaign now demands disclosure, and the 2027 race makes it a political fight. The structural why: oil-backed loans mortgage future barrels, and their terms move with Brent crude. Frame the demand as a campaign's, and lead with what the public cannot see.

stories.label: Microsoft outage hits tens of thousands of users
stories.summary: Outlook, Teams and Microsoft 365 went down for hours across continents. Microsoft's early explanation is that some servers became 'unexpectedly unavailable', which overloaded the rest. Lead with the systemic risk: a single vendor's capacity failure halts email and work for governments and firms worldwide. The reader is technical, so explain why a loss of headroom cascades. Sources from the UK, India, Qatar and Malaysia show the global reach.

stories.label: Nvidia privately confirmed it could track chips to fight smuggling, even as industry publicly questioned feasibility
stories.summary: Not the resignation, which is already covered, but what it brings back into view: Nvidia representatives privately told Rep. Bill Foster that the Chip Security Act's location-tracking requirement was feasible, while the industry argued in public that it was not. Lead with the gap between what Nvidia said in private and in public. The structural why: export controls on AI chips to China depend on verification Nvidia said it could provide, and Huang's exit over an alleged Chinese spy revives the bill.

stories.label: Google rolls out Gemini 4 Hydrogen, finally replacing 3.8 Flash
stories.summary: Google ships Gemini 4 Hydrogen, the cheap high-volume model that replaces 3.8 Flash, as a broad release, unlike the staged, security-gated launches of its larger siblings Carbon and Argon. Lead with that contrast: the model most developers will actually call skipped the cautious rollout. Explain what it replaces and the cost and capability trade-off for developers.

stories.label: Analyse des Koalitionsvertrages: Automatisierte Datenanalyse kommt auch in Mecklenburg-Vorpommern
stories.summary: Mecklenburg-Vorpommern's new SPD-Left-Green coalition rules out Palantir and backs open source, yet its coalition agreement still brings automated police data analysis to the state. Lead with the paradox: even a left-wing government adopts the surveillance tool and only changes the vendor. The structural why: German states are adopting automated police analytics one by one despite the 2023 constitutional court limits, so rejecting a vendor is not rejecting the practice.
